hypothesis: Second half of the claim: mouse learning-or-memory genes are over-represented among genes whose mutants show cancer, regeneration or embryogenesis phenotypes, beyond what their depth of phenotyping explains.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered: for each of the three outcome categories (cancer, regeneration, embryogenesis), the Mantel-Haenszel odds ratio of the learning-or-memory set versus the outcome set, stratified by deciles of each gene's number of distinct MP phenotype terms, is > 1.5 with one-sided Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel p < 0.001. The claim is supported if all three pass.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered: the claim is refuted if the stratified odds ratio is <= 1.2 or p >= 0.05 in at least two of the three categories. Any other outcome (for example one or two categories pass) is 'mixed'. Unstratified odds ratios and raw counts ('memory genes appear at all') are reported but are not decisive, because almost any well-studied gene set 'appears' in large phenotype catalogues.
interpretation: 'Genetic studies of cancer, regeneration and embryogenesis' are operationalised as mouse mutant phenotypes curated by MGI (MGI_GenePheno.rpt: genotypes with a mutation in one marker), mapped to genes by MGI marker ID. Outcome sets, each with all MP is_a descendants: cancer = MP:0002006 neoplasm; embryogenesis = MP:0001672 abnormal embryo development or MP:0008762 embryonic lethality; regeneration = every MP term whose label contains 'regenerat' (MP has no single regeneration parent; this includes e.g. MP:0002658 abnormal liver regeneration, MP:0000750 abnormal muscle regeneration, MP:0004858 abnormal nervous system regeneration). 'Memory genes' are defined as in the first-half test (claim-tests/levin-papers/levin-2022-tame-19): GO:0007611 learning or memory and descendants, experimental evidence codes only, so the memory set is defined independently of the MP outcome annotations. The universe is genes with at least one MP annotation in MGI_GenePheno.rpt and at least one experimental GO BP annotation. The claim's second half has no 'beyond ion channels' qualifier, so the primary analysis does not exclude channel or synaptic genes; the first-half exclusion is repeated as a secondary analysis. Secondary analyses also report the same test with the memory set defined genetically by MP:0002063 abnormal learning/memory/conditioning, and stratified by GO experimental BP depth instead of MP depth. Secondary analyses do not change the verdict.
